2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that, one Md Solaiman and 2 (two) others, as plaintiffs, had filed Title Suit No.354 of 2006, before the court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayangonj, against Md Hazrat Ali and 7 (seven) others, seeking declaration of title in respect of 16 annas property described in the schedule to the plaint and for correction of RS khatian No. 53 plot No 10 of Mouza Dighiborab PS Rupgonj, District-Narayangonj so far as it relates to entering the name of Md Fozor Ali and others. The case of the plaintiffs is that, the CS recorded owner of the suit plot was one Atorjan Bibi, who died leaving 2(two) sons 2(two) daughters namely, (1) Warif, (2) Abdul Gafur, (3) Atori Bibi and (4) Sabuja Bibi. The further case of the plaintiffs as stated in paragraph Nos. 3 to 5 of the plaint is that, the plaintiffs have derived title in the suit property measuring 0.1930 acres (19.30 decimals) of land out of 0.2900 acres (29 decimals) of land from the other heirs of CS recorded owners Atorjan Bibi excepting Warif @ Warish in the manner as described in paragraph No. 3 to 5 of the plaint. In paragraph No. 6, the plaintiffs described their cause of action for filing the suit. 

 8. Learned Advocates Mr AFM Mesbah-uddin Ahmed, Mr Subrata Saha and Mr Kamal Hossain appeared for the petitioner. Having placed the petition along with oral and documen-tary evidences the learned Advocates first of all submit that, the plaintiffs have denied title from the heirs of a son from their bia, who got title from daughters of Abdul Gafur (one sons of CS recorded owner Atorjan Bibi and from Saburun Nessa, daughter of Sabuja Bibi, one of the two daughters of the said CS recorded owner Atorjan Bibi). Their further contention is that no record of right could be produced in the name of Warish (one of sons of CS recorded owner Atorjan Bibi) as the case of the plaintiffs. Their further contention is that, although the name of their bia were rightly recorded in RS khatian No. 53, however, against RS plot No. 10, name of Md Fazor All and others as permitted by Abdul Malek has been wrongly recorded and that has created cloud in respect of title of the plaintiffs in the suit property, therefore, they have prayed for declaration of title in the suit property as well as the correction of wrong recording of name of Md Fazor Ali and others against RS plot No. 10 has been challenged other correction of the RS khatian No. 553, vide prayer Kha to the plaint. The learned Advocates submit that, the trial court has rightly discussed oral and documentary evidence on record and decreed the suit upon proper assessment of the case of the parties, but the appellate court, having failed to appreciate the case of the parties and assessing the evidence on record has passed the impugned judgment and decree and therefore, it has committed grave error of law causing serious prejudiced as regard the burden of proof. The learned Advocates has referred the decisions, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 26 between: Ishaque (Md) vs Ekramul Hague Chowdhury decision, reported in 1987 BLD (AD) 103 between: Chinibash Pramanik vs Nurul Hossain Mollah. They conclude that, this Rule has merit and the same may kindly be made absolute. 

 9. On the other hand, learned Advocates Mr Abdul Quayum with Mr Tapan Kumar Biswas with Mr Md Moklesur Rahman with Mr M Saifuddin Khokon with Mr Mohammad Golam Kibria, Advocates appeared on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2. Their main contention is that, there is no iota of evidence to prove the case of the plaintiffs that, the CS recorded owner Atorjan Bibi died leaving 2(two) sons 2(two) daughters namely, (1) Warish, (2) Abdul Gafur, (3) Atori Bibi and (4) Sabuja Bibi as narrated in the plaint. Indeed, Atorjan Bibi died leaving only one son namely, Warish as the sole owner of the 16 annas property to the suit land. The learned Advocates very strenuously argued that invention of another son and 2(two) daughters namely, (1) Atori Bibi and (2) Sabuja Bibi of the CS recorded owner is totally absurd and false and also concocted story. They maintain that, this Abdul Gafur, Atori Bibi and Sabuja Bibi exists only in the pleadings of the plaintiffs, but not in reality. They pointed out that, the CS recorded owner Atorjan Bibi died leaving only one son Warish, who is the owner of 0.29 acre of land (29 decimals) and had sold the same to Md Fozor Ali in the year 1936, vide registered deed No. 2068 dated 11-6-1936 (Exbihit E). The learned Advocates clarified that, since the kabala Exhibit-E was executed and registered in the year 1936, at that time SA operation did not took place and since the property was sold, therefore, the SA khatian No. 455 containing the suit plot No. 33 and others, name of Md Fazor Ali has been duly recorded in the name of Md Fazor Ali [Exbihit Ka(1)] and said Md Fazor Ali sold his 0.29 acre of land by 3(three) separate kabalas and by sale deed No. 4653 dated 19-12-1972 Exhibit Kha, whereby he has sold 0.1450 acre (14.50 decimals) of land to Abdul Malek and to Hasna Hena Dewan, vide registered deed No. 6679 dated 24-4-1983 Exhibit-G, whereby Md Fazor Ali had sold 0.0650 acre of land to one Md Ibrahim Miah, vide deed 3420 dated 8-9-1982 (Exbihit F) and he has also sold 0.08 acre of land to Abdul Malek Miah and Md Ibrahim Miah and by this way the defendant got title in the suit property, vide 3(three) sale deeds, marked as Exhibit E(1), Exhibit-I and Exhibit F(1), respectively. Their further case is that, 0.29 acre of land was acquired by the Government (both the parties admits) and the rest 20 decimals of land has been duly recorded in the RS khatian No. 53 of Mouza Dighibora of PS Rubgonj District: Narayangonj against RS plot No. 10 as recorded in the comment column of the said khatain along with the name of Md Fazor Ali and Abdul Malek. However, the learned Advocates for the OP Nos. 1 and 2 also submit that, since the plaintiff has filed a mutation case based on their fake deeds, false and baseless title, therefore, the defendant could have been filed a mutation case and the said case could not be finalized. But, this delay in getting mutation on the basis of mutation case does not confer title of the defendants as has been held by the High Court Division in a case, reported in 20 DLR 1019 Between: SM Lutfullah vs Bibi Badrunnessa and others, wherein it has been held that, "so far as the legality of the mutation effected, it is sufficient to state that this is merely an executive order which cannot confer title". The learned Advocates, therefore, sums up that, the facts and pleadings considered in the light of the entire evidence on record clearly shows that, the CS recorded owner Atorjan Bibi died leaving only one son namely, Warish and the chain of title begun from Warish, which is stand and proved by the defendants, derived title of the suit property, which the appellate court has properly appreciated in its judgment. Similarly, the appellate court has also assessing the evidence on record independently allowed the appeal and reversed the findings of the trial court and in passing the impugned judgment and decree, the appellate court has committed no error of law and facts and there is no misreading of evidence or non-reading of evidence. They conclude that, this Rule has no merit and the same may kindly be discharged. 

 11. I find that, there is no iota of evidence to prove the case of the plaintiff that, the CS recorded owner Atorjan Bibi died leaving 2(two) sons and 2(two) daughters namely, (1) Warif, (2) Abdul Gafur, (3) Atori Bibi and (4) Sabuja Bibi as narrated in the plaint. Indeed, Atorjan Bibi died leaving only one son namely, Warish as the sole owner of the 16 annas property to the suit land. The invention of another son and 2(two) daughters namely, (1) Atori Bibi and (2) Sabuja Bibi of the CS recorded owner could not be proved by the plaintiffs. It also appears thar, Abdul Gafur, Atori Bibi and Sabuja Bibi exists only in the pleadings of the plaintiffs, but not in reality and the CS recorded owner Atorjan Bibi died leaving only one son, named Warish, who is the owner of 0.29 acres of land (29 decimals) and had sold the same to Md Fozor Ali in the year 1936, vide registered deed No. 2068 dated 11-6-1936 (Exbihit E). The kabala (Exhibit-E) was executed and registered in the year 1936. At that time SA operation did not took place and since the property was sold, therefore, the SA khatian No. 455 containing the suit plot No. 33, name of Md Fazor Ali has been duly recorded, alongwith others [Exbihit Ka(1)], during SA operation and said Md Fazor Ali sold his 0.29 acre of land by 3(three) separate kabala and by sale deed No. 4653 dated 19-12-1972 (Exbihit Kha), whereby he has sold 0.1450 acre (14.50 decimals) of land to Abdul Malek and to Hasna Hena Dewan, vide registered deed No. 6679 dated 24-4-1983 (Exbihit G), whereby Md Fazor Ali had sold 0.0650 acre of land to one Md Ibrahim Miah, vide deed 3420 dated 08-9-1982 (Exbihit F) and he has also sold 0.08 acre of land to Abdul Malek Miah and Md Ibrahim Miah and by this way the defendant got title in the suit property, vide 3(three) sale deed marked as Exhibit E(1), Exhibit-I and Exhibit F(1). Their further case that, 0.29 acre of land was acquired by the Government (both the parties admits) and the rest 20 decimals of land has been duly recorded in the RS khatian No. 53 of Mouza Dighibora of PS Rubgonj District: Narayangonj against RS plot No. 10, recorded in the comment column of the said khatain alongwith the name of Md Fazor Ali and Abdul Malek. However, the plaintiff has filed a mutation case based on their fake deeds and baseless title; therefore, the defendant's mutation case could not be finalized. But, this delay in getting mutation does not confer title of the defendants as has been held by the High Court Division in a case, reported in 20 DLR 1019 between: SM Lutfullah vs Bibi Badrunnessa and others, wherein it has been held that, "so far as the legality of the mutation effected, it is sufficient to state that this is merely an executive order which cannot confer title".
